predecessors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Ifriqiya: 'After the Fatimids moved to Egypt in 972, he was appointed viceroy of Ifriqiya'

successors.name: Kingdom of Africa
successors.text: Mahdia, Sousse, Sfax and Gabes, taken by the Normans of Sicily in June-July 1148

ledger.x: 972: Buluggin ibn Ziri becomes viceroy of Ifriqiya for the Fatimids.
978: the Fatimids grant Buluggin 'overlordship of Tripolitania'.
980: Buluggin conquers Fez and the western Maghreb.
ledger.cp: western Maghreb rulers (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1017: the central Maghreb round Ashir is lost to the Hammadids.
1052: the Zirids are routed by the Arab nomads.
1057: the interior is abandoned to the nomads (see the loss event); the contest ends because the Zirids no longer hold it.
1057: the capital moves from al-Mansuriyya to Mahdia.
1059: Tunis passes to the Banu Khurasan.
1146: the Norman capture of Tripoli ends whatever Zirid overlordship remained: 'In 1146 he successfully besieged it'.
1148: Sousse surrenders on 1 July without a fight to the Norman fleet.
1148: the Zirid dynasty ends with the fall of Sfax on 12 July.

wars.name: Zirid-Hammadid War
wars.outcome: Hammad's rebellion succeeds: a 1017 peace let him keep effective independence.

wars.name: Zirid intervention in Sicily
wars.outcome: 'In 1036, Sicilian Muslims asked al-Mu'izz for help against Kalbid emir al-Akhal.

wars.name: Battle of Haydaran and the Hilalian invasion
wars.outcome: Zirid defeat at Haydaran on 14 April 1052; Kairouan abandoned in 1057; the dynasty survives on the coast at Mahdia.

wars.name: Norman conquest of the Zirid coast
wars.outcome: Djerba 1135, Mahdia a protectorate of Sicily by 1142, Tripoli 1146, Mahdia 22 June 1148, Sousse 1 July, Sfax 12 July; the Zirid dynasty ends in 1148.

wars.name: Zirid conquest of the western Maghreb
wars.outcome: 'By 980 he had conquered Fez and most of the western Maghreb'; Buluggin died at Sijilmasa in 984 and 'his successor abandoned Morocco in 985'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages opened: the interior of Ifriqiya was nomad and Hilalian country after 1052, the Ashir frontier was a governorate boundary until 1015, and the coast is the only fixed edge.
